source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary
source.citation: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (Oxford); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 Hermeneia; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (Oxford, PD); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford); Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition; Reed 2005 Fallen Angels.
source.paleography_note: The layered-witness convention reflects the manuscript-attestation reality: Aramaic DSS fragments are FRAGMENTARY (preserve only portions of chs 1-36); Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus preserves chs 1-32 substantially complete; Ge'ez is the only complete witness but the most distant in time and language from the Aramaic original. Per-verse selection prioritizes the oldest preserved witness; alternate witnesses documented where they differ materially or provide cross-collation value.

verses.text_greek: Ἀπὸ ἡμέρας τοῦ καιροῦ τῆς σφαγῆς καὶ ἀπωλείας καὶ θανάτου τῶν γιγάντων, οἱ ὁπόθεν τὰ πνεύματα ἐξεληλύθασιν, οἱ καταισχύνοντες ἀπολῶνται· καὶ μέχρι ἡμέρας τελειώσεως τῆς κρίσεως τῆς μεγάλης, ἐν ᾗ ὁ αἰὼν ὁ μέγας τελεσθήσεται, ἅμα τοῖς Ἐγρηγόροις καὶ ἀσεβέσιν, τελεσθήσεται.
verses.translit: Apo hēmeras tou kairou tēs sphagēs kai apōleias kai thanatou tōn gigantōn, hoi hopothen ta pneumata exelēlythasin, hoi kataischynontes apolountai; kai mechri hēmeras teleiōseōs tēs kriseōs tēs megalēs, en hē ho aiōn ho megas telesthēsetai, hama tois Egrēgorois kai asebesin, telesthēsetai.
verses.text_geez: እምዕለተ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ኅርደት፡ ወሕጕለት፡ ወሞተ፡ ሬማ፡ እመኒ፡ ወፅኡ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ዘያኀስሩ፡ ይትኀጐሉ፡ ወእስከ፡ ዕለተ፡ ፍጻሜ፡ ኵነኔ፡ ዐባይ፡ በዘይትፌጸም፡ ዓለም፡ ዐቢይ፡ ኅቡረ፡ ምስለ፡ ትጉሃን፡ ወረሲዓን፡ ይትፌጸም፡
verses.notes: Continuation of the giants→demons etiology. The 'great judgment day' formula closes the temporal arc.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ νῦν τοῖς Ἐγρηγόροις, οἵτινες ἀπέστειλάν σε ἐρωτῆσαι περὶ αὐτῶν, οἵτινες τὸ πρῶτον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἦσαν, εἰπέ·
verses.translit: Kai nyn tois Egrēgorois, hoitines apesteilan se erōtēsai peri autōn, hoitines to prōton en tō ouranō ēsan, eipe;
verses.text_geez: ወይእዜኒ፡ ለትጉሃን፡ እለ፡ ፈነዉከ፡ ከመ፡ ትስአል፡ በእንቲአሆሙ፡ እለ፡ ቀዳሚ፡ በውስተ፡ ሰማይ፡ ሀለዉ፡ በሎሙ፡
verses.notes: Enoch's commission to deliver verdict to the Watchers — repetition for emphasis.

verses.text_greek: Ὑμεῖς ἦτε ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ πᾶν μυστήριον ὃ οὐκ ἀνεκαλύφθη ὑμῖν, καὶ μυστήριον τὸ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ γεγονὸς ἔγνωτε, καὶ τοῦτο ἐμηνύσατε ταῖς γυναιξὶν ἐν τῇ σκληροκαρδίᾳ ὑμῶν, καὶ ἐν τῷ μυστηρίῳ τούτῳ πληθύνουσιν αἱ θήλειαι καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὰ κακὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: Hymeis ēte en tō ouranō, kai pan mystērion ho ouk anekalyphthē hymin, kai mystērion to ek tou theou gegonos egnōte, kai touto emēnysate tais gynaixin en tē sklērokardia hymōn, kai en tō mystēriō toutō plēthynousin hai thēleiai kai hoi anthrōpoi ta kaka epi tēs gēs.
verses.text_geez: አንትሙ፡ ሀሎክሙ፡ በሰማይ፡ ወኵሉ፡ ምሥጢር፡ ዘኢተከሥተ፡ ለክሙ፡ ወምሥጢር፡ ዘእምኀበ፡ እግዚአብሔር፡ ኮነ፡ አአመርክሙ፡ ወዘንተ፡ ነገርክሙ፡ ለአንስት፡ በድርቀተ፡ ልብክሙ፡ ወበዝ፡ ምሥጢር፡ ይበዝኁ፡ አንስት፡ ወሰብእ፡ እኩየ፡ ላዕለ፡ ምድር፡
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK + CANON-ENGAGEMENT SITE.** The 'mystery from God' that the Watchers knew and revealed to women. The mystērion that 'multiplies evil on the earth' — the canon's central interest. The text frames knowledge-transfer as the original-sin variant. **CRITICAL NUANCE**: 'every mystery which was not revealed to you' — implying that some mysteries WERE properly revealed to them; the violation was revealing what was NOT theirs to reveal. This nuance matters for the knowledge-transmission framing. cf. 1 Cor 2:7-10.

verses.text_greek: Λέγε αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἔσται ὑμῖν εἰρήνη.
verses.translit: Lege autois; Ouk estai hymin eirēnē.
verses.notes: Closing sentence: 'no peace for you' — the formula repeated, sealing the Watchers' judgment. Closes the Watchers-myth narrative arc (chs 6-16). The next narrative unit (chs 17-36) is Enoch's cosmic-tours.
